out.in_your_terms: At 1,000 a day, free users get the same allowance they had in v1, and serving costs stay predictable. Raising it to 5,000 gives hobbyists and people evaluating the API much more room, and sales thinks that would help us compete. It would cost about $600 a month more at current signups, and that figure would grow with adoption. Finance hasn't weighed in, and once a higher free limit is public, lowering it later would upset users.

send_down.instruction: Set the v2 free tier to 1,000 requests/day, matching v1, and unblock the dependent agent. Any customer-facing docs or announcement of the limit must go to Jordan before publishing.
Set the v2 free tier to 5,000 requests/day, and record the roughly $600/month serving-cost increase for finance. Route any public docs or announcement of the limit to Jordan before it goes out.
